questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A high quality university, that was placed somewhat centrally in my desired city. I also had a personal interest in the culture in Korea, which also affected my search in destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Fairly easy. The university International office would send out emails with necessary information, however they were sometimes send out at the last minute. I would suggest joining the big Exchange Student group chat on Kakao to find more information.

As to the arrival in the airport I made sure to double check that I had all the necessary documents, through the korean embassy and through YouTube guides (the Corona rules were updated regularly and many travel youtubers would make updated videos on  these procedures).

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not need any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation was good, and you got a pamphlet with most of the information you could need. After the orientation there was a Buddies Night Intro party with a dinner before. I would suggest going to this, especially the dinner, if you want to meet other exchange students, especially if you live off campus and don't get to meet others at the dorms.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing on airbnb. There are many different places to stay in the areas near the university, all of differing quality. I would suggest finding a place either in Sinchon or Hongdae, both of which is I walking distance from the university main gates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be harder just randomly finding other exchange students to hang out with compared to if you're living in the dorms, so you need to put in an extra effort to meet need people. However, it is very nice to have your own place without a roommate, and there should be less rules like curfews etc. compared to living in the dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had a certain amount of points (miles) to allot between then classes that you wanted to take. You could prioritise the certain classes by adding more points to these, giving you a greater chance to get the class. I found this to be a good system as it wasn't based on first come first served, but on prioritising you classes with points. That way you didn't have to compete with the regular students who have a greater knowledge of the system, in order to get your classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an information pamphlet that explained the system and how to allot points. I would suggest to read this through thoroughly. Other than that I'm not sure, as I didn't need further help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would suggest knowing what classes you want to take, in what time slots, and what their codes are beforehand. Write them down, so that you can easily just copy paste them into the system. Also check out how many points students in the previous year allotted to the specific classes to give you a guideline as to how many you should give them in order to get the class.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most of my classes were good and taught well, however, they are taught at the mercy of the professor, and you might not get through the entire syllabus.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3rd and 4th year classes, both of which was on a level comparable to the final year of the the KU bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some classes were taught with lectures as we know them from KU, however, there were no exercise based classes to assist the lectures, which was something I personally missed. Other classes were taught as a lecture and exercise class combined which was not the best way of teaching in my opinion.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Virus and Host
Immunology
Korean 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all exchange students to take the basic language course (korean 1). It will make you much more confident in getting around and speaking korean to the local community.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Hospital visit that was covered by insurance, but I had to pay up front myself.

Fees for ARC application, and for NHIS if you don't get excempt.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport is super cheap, a trip around Seoul using the buses and the metro normally costs around 7 DKK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is the Buddies program, which is where you get a mentor, and get to meet other exchange students.

There are many different clubs you can join, just beware that some do not accept international students or don't accept exchange students staying for only one semester. You can ask them at the club fair.

There were also a Global program where you could join cooking classes, dance classes, day trips etc. This is explained at the orientation.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend the Buddies program (good to meet other exchange students), the Yonsei English Society (good to meet korean and international students), and some of the global classes (good to immerse yourself in korean culture).

Also there are many different group chats on Kakao you can join, such as hiking or getting dinner together.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on day trips or weekend trips around the country. I would suggest finding time to go to Busan and Jeju Island. I also went to Ulsan and Gyeongju both beautiful places.

I would also suggest to try to see as much in Seoul as possible, such as Namsan tower, Bukhansan, and Lotte World.

The weekends are also a good time to go eat Kbbq and go partying in Hongdae and Itaewon, or go to cute cafes and stores.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy, my only issue was finding out what to eat for breakfast..

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs with both international and korean students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That it is somewhat unusual to eat dinner alone, and many places you need to be 2 or more people to eat.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people could respect your private space and that everything was open quite late. It made it seem like Seoul was always alive and it made me feel very safe that there were always people around on the streets.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for your ARC as early as possible (you can apply through yonsei but it takes longer to arrive), make sure your student id works in the library (it is the best place for serious studying, but sometimes the id doesn't work and you need to get a new one issued), and join as many activities provided at the University as possible!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not host institution but important nonetheless: If your credit or debit cards for some reason doesn't work, it is possible to get a prepaid debit card from a vending machine called Namane. It really saved me many times, as my card kept on getting declined in stores. The vending machines are located at major stations and there is one in Hongdae in a book store.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and experiencing the Yonsei culture. The students have a lot of pride in their university and they have an ongoing rivalry with Korea University, which results in the Yonko games (I would suggest going to the baseball game it was really great also if you don't usually watch sports games).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier and always seeming like the odd one out. You do however get used to it fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
